why:
Harvested rather than staged: every other fixture is under the 40-step cap that `episode._MAX_STEPS` imposes on what the sift model reads, so nothing exercised the truncation. The slice runs from the start of a real article-writing session to its first marker.

Two tasks. The first prompt asks how to share work with a second Claude account and is answered; the remaining twelve are all one job — assemble the article, draft and rate titles, restructure the sections, set up a comment workflow — ending in the file being handed over. Ground truth is 2.
history:
Three things this is the first fixture to cover.

1. It exceeds the sift cap. 92 substantive steps render as 40 plus '… and 52 more steps', so the model judging reusability sees 43% of the procedure. No other fixture reaches the cap.

2. Its marker is a `SendUserFile`, not a commit — the artifact-handover half of `is_marker` firing on real work for the first time. Every other live fixture ends in git.

3. It is the session-1 over-merge at scale: 13 prompts folded into one 92-step episode because a single handover sits at the end. `241955c7` shows the same shape with 4 prompts; this shows there is no ceiling on it.

The full session, unsliced, segments into 74 episodes and banks 67 candidates from one sitting — worth knowing before anyone reasons about ledger volume from the small fixtures.
expected_fail: Segments into 1 episode against a ground truth of 2 — the account question is folded into the article work by `_absorb_before_commit`, which has one handover to absorb into and 13 prompts' worth of work to absorb. Same defect as `241955c7`, four times the size.
